newsitem.title: CHINA: DEBTS OWED TO CHINA STATE FIRMS SURGES BY END-MAY.
newsitem.headline: DEBTS OWED TO CHINA STATE FIRMS SURGES BY END-MAY.

text.p: China's big state enterprises were owed 328.594 billion yuan ($39.59 billion) at the end of May, a three-fold increase on the year, Shanghai's official Business News said on Monday.

Accounts receivable of state enterprises surged in the first half of this year due to many firms using the tally system in a bid to reduce stocks, the newspaper said. The tally system allows buyers to take products on credit and pay the debts later.
According to a survey of 5,000 medium and large state firms by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, total net accounts receivable was 328.594 billion yuan by the end of May, it said.

Buyers were also slower to pay back the debts, the newspaper said. The liquidity of accounts receivable fell to an average 73 days per cycle, five days slower compared with the beginning of this year, it said.
